panels.sample_scope: Supplementary Fig. 19 | Environmental evolution around the trough preceding a near-peak return. a, Recorded wind intensity. b–f, Mid-level relative humidity, 200–850 hPa shear, sea-surface temperature, potential intensity (PI) and PI − V in the 200–800 km annulus. Time zero is the last wind minimum between a temporary departure and its next qualifying return. Lines show means after averaging events within each SID; shaded bands are pointwise 95% intervals from 2,000 SID bootstrap draws. The fixed time window retains subsequent observed records, including those after return, and is not uniformly a reintensification phase. Of 123 cyclones with 133 returns, 25 cyclones still lie within their actual trough-to-return interval at +24 h. Availability is diagnostic-specific and reported by time in the accompanying source data; PI and PI − V require valid thermodynamic profiles. Tables S8a,b,d,k report the pre-trough states, actual trough-to-return endpoint changes, comparable-wind comparisons and common-support PI − V components.
